cards.title: Ancient is relative
cards.text: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza. The pyramid was about 2,500 years old by her lifetime.

cards.title: Older than empires
cards.text: The University of Oxford was already teaching students by 1096, more than two centuries before the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325.

cards.title: Movable type
cards.text: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press, developed around 1440 in Mainz, helped make books cheap enough to spread literacy across Europe.

cards.title: The shortest war
cards.text: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 is often called the shortest war in recorded history: it lasted roughly 40 minutes.

cards.question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
cards.explanation: The border opened on 9 November 1989; Germany reunified in October 1990.

cards.question: The Magna Carta was sealed in 1215 by which English king?
Who was the first emperor of a unified China?
cards.explanation: He unified China in 221 BCE; he is also known for the Terracotta Army.

cards.question: Which mission first landed humans on the Moon?
cards.explanation: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed on 20 July 1969.

cards.statement: Viking warriors wore horned helmets into battle.
cards.explanation: No horned Viking battle helmet has ever been found. The image comes largely from 19th-century costume designs for Wagner's operas.
He was about 1.69 m (5 ft 7 in), average or slightly above for a Frenchman of his time. Confusion between French and English inches helped the myth.

cards.statement: Educated Europeans in Columbus's time believed the Earth was flat.
cards.explanation: Scholars had known the Earth was round since ancient Greece; the debate was about its size.

cards.statement: The Hundred Years' War lasted exactly 100 years.
cards.explanation: It ran from 1337 to 1453: 116 years, with long truces in between.

cards.statement: Egypt's great pyramids were built mainly by enslaved people.
cards.explanation: Archaeological evidence from workers' villages suggests paid, organised labourers who were fed and given medical care.
The Great Pyramid was the tallest human-made structure for nearly 4,000 years.
